subject.title: [RFC] Context Provenance: Add source/volatility metadata to injected context segments

question: Should OpenClaw pursue model-visible inline provenance tags for injected context segments now, or prefer a runtime/context-engine provenance contract before changing prompt text?
rationale: The source proves the requested behavior is still missing, but the right design affects prompt bytes, cache stability, model instructions, memory surfaces, and possible config shape, so automation should not choose the product direction while a same-author implementation PR is already open.

options.title: Review linked Phase 1 first
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/54830 as the concrete decision point for whether inline bootstrap provenance tags should exist, then split later phases into follow-ups if accepted.

options.title: Prefer runtime provenance first
options.body: Decline inline prompt tags for now and steer remaining work toward structured ContextEngine/InputProvenance contracts such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82137.

options.title: Sponsor broader freshness design
options.body: Keep this RFC open but require a wider design that covers memory freshness, prompt caching, and deterministic refresh before any implementation lands.

recommendation.title: Review linked Phase 1 first
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/54830 as the concrete decision point for whether inline bootstrap provenance tags should exist, then split later phases into follow-ups if accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties Vincent Koc to the prompt-cache and Project Context ordering surface most affected by inline provenance tags.
